conversations.title: Parkinson’s drastically changed how they have sex. They're not alone.
conversations.reply: Parkinson's doesn't get to define your sex life, but let's be real, it's a mood killer when your meds wear off mid-session. Disabled people have love lives, and they're not all rainbows and unicorns.

conversations.title: Forget Tinder: LinkedIn is the new place to find love
conversations.reply: LinkedIn, where the only thing more abundant than potential matches is the humblebrag about your 'disrupting the industry' startup. Good luck finding love among the networking events.

conversations.title: You May Be In A 'Tolyamorous’ Relationship Without Ever Having Discussed It
conversations.reply: Tolyamory, because who needs labels when you can just wing it and hope your partner doesn't notice the 3am Tinder swipes.

conversations.title: FCM Travel caution over accessibility of new digital arrival cards
conversations.reply: Digital arrival cards, because what's more fun than trying to navigate a website with a screen reader while jet-lagged?

conversations.title: Lover, Not a Fighter and Real Feelings: Why Gen Z Romance Is Getting More Honest
conversations.reply: Gen Z romance, where the only thing more exhausting than the dating scene is the constant need to present a curated Instagram feed.

conversations.title: Column | Asking Eric: Neighbors react badly to person with autism disorder
conversations.reply: Neighborly love, where the only thing more abundant than bad advice is the assumption that you're just being 'too sensitive'.

conversations.title: Midnight social media curfew proposed for older UK teens
conversations.reply: Because what every teenager needs is a bedtime, courtesy of the UK government, because clearly, they're the experts on being cool.

conversations.title: The founder of Hinge raised $18M to build a new AI dating service, Overtone
conversations.reply: AI dating, because who needs human intuition when you can just let an algorithm decide your love life, and hopefully, it won't suggest your cousin.

moment: It's Disability Pride Month, and I'm celebrating by reminding everyone that disabled people have love lives, and they're not all tragic or inspirational ,  sometimes they're just plain messy, and that's okay.
